notes: OUR OWN local measurements of Mapika decider-2b v11 (Q8_0 GGUF) and decider-4b v2.1 (Q4_K_M GGUF) on one busy Ryzen 9 7900X (CPU only, 8 threads, load average 11-21), 2026-10-03; raw JSON in ~/.tmp/decisions-design/bench/r_*.json. Evidence grade D by design: one machine, background load, 5 timed repeats, a single Daisy agent-state scenario (461 tokens; requests 596-940 input tokens), 12 basic cases. Latency rows carry vantage local_cpu. Input tokens are what the engine reported (usage.input_tokens). Packing questions into one row (independent=False) is faster but changed probabilities (e.g. P(violates policy) 0.266 -> 0.094 on 2B, urgency 0.46 -> 0.89 on 4B): see caveats. decider-ai GGUF engine has no prefix cache and imports torch even on the GGUF path.

claims.statement: Local CPU summary (our measurements, busy box): decider-2b v11 Q8_0 answers short states (<= 40 tokens) in about 0.2 s median (220 ms, max 288 ms) and a 696-token request with 12 described options in about 2.8 s; decider-4b v2.1 Q4_K_M is about twice as slow (440 ms and 5.3 s) and uses about twice the RAM (2B: 2.6 GB RSS after load, 4B: 5.0 GB). On one hard agent decision ("which tool first": the video must go through bg_run, a reminder is pending, the user asks about the weather) 2B picked job_status (0.45) and gave P(sending without checking violates policy) 0.27, while 4B picked bg_run_video (0.88) and gave 0.97. One example, not a benchmark.
claims.implication: Short-state routing is feasible on CPU with 2B; anything near 700 tokens costs seconds. Prefer the 4B for non-trivial agent decisions.

claims.statement: Packing four mixed questions into one row (independent=False) cut latency 5.6x (2B 16.4 s -> 2.9 s, 4B 30.1 s -> 6.1 s) but CHANGED answers: 2B P(violates_policy) 0.266 -> 0.094, urgency score 1.1 -> 0.91; 4B urgency 0.46 -> 0.89, P(needs_background) 0.709 -> 0.851. Priming the shared prefix in llama-server got independent semantics at 4,250 ms first / 2,798 ms warm (about 3-4x faster than cold independent) with max probability difference 0.0176 vs the in-process readout and the same argmax.
claims.implication: Compare packed vs primed-independent, not packed vs cold-independent; test packed vs singleton probabilities before relying on packing.

claims.statement: A stock llama-server reproduces the decider readout: send token ids up to the answer slot with n_predict 1 and n_probs 100, then softmax the letter log-probs by the per-type temperature; maximum absolute probability difference 0.0036 vs the in-process readout with the same argmax on all three scenarios (v11 temperatures: choice 1.164, noul 1.624, score 1.124). Q8_0 equals bf16 within noise per the model card.
